cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Angiosperms undergo unique Double Fertilization: pollen grain germinates on stigma, discharging two sperm nuclei down the pollen tube into embryo sac. First sperm fertilizes egg cell forming diploid zygote (2n -> embryo); second sperm fuses with two polar nuclei forming triploid Primary Endosperm Nucleus (3n -> nutritive endosperm).
• Global Context Focus: *Fairness and development (resource sustainability and ethical responsibility)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$\text{Sperm } (n) + \text{Egg } (n) \rightarrow \text{Zygote } (2n), \quad \text{Sperm } (n) + 2\,\text{Polar Nuclei } (2n) \rightarrow \text{Endosperm } (3n)$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: Post-fertilization: Ovary matures into the fruit; Ovules develop into seeds.
• Dynamic Mechanism: Zygote develops into embryo with cotyledons, plumule (future shoot), and radicle (future root).
• Quantitative Relationship: Endosperm provides nourishment to the developing embryo until green photosynthetic leaves emerge.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:
• Inquirer & Thinker: Packing a lunchbox for a newborn: one key event creates the baby (zygote embryo), while the simultaneous second event packs a rich lunchbox of food (triploid endosperm) to feed the baby during seed germination.
• Real-World Inquiry: Hybrid seed agricultural corporations breed polyploid crops (like seedless triploid watermelons) using pollination manipulation.

• Criterion B (Inquiring and Designing): Planning controlled biological experiments and sampling methodologies.

cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Human sexual reproduction involves specialized gametogenesis: Male testes produce sperm and testosterone; Female ovaries produce ova and estrogen/progesterone. The 28-day menstrual cycle involves follicular phase (estrogen rises, endometrium thickens), ovulation (LH surge at day 14), and luteal phase (progesterone maintains uterine lining for embryo implantation).
• Global Context Focus: *Globalization and sustainability (interconnected global cycles and human impact)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$\text{Cycle: Menstrual (Days 1-5)} \rightarrow \text{Follicular} \rightarrow \text{Ovulation (Day 14, LH Surge)} \rightarrow \text{Luteal (Progesterone)}$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: Fertilization takes place in the ampulla of the Fallopian tube (oviduct).
• Dynamic Mechanism: Implantation of the blastocyst occurs in the vascularized endometrium of the uterus.
• Quantitative Relationship: Placenta acts as the physiological organ of exchange for nutrients, gases, and waste between maternal and fetal bloodstreams.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:
• Inquirer & Thinker: Renovating a nursery room every month: the uterine lining builds a plush, blood-rich bed (endometrium) in anticipation of a baby; if no fertilized egg arrives, the room is cleared out (menstruation) to rebuild fresh next month.
• Real-World Inquiry: In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) reproductive clinics culture fertilized blastocysts in vitro before transferring them directly to the uterine cavity.

cheatSheet.title: Contraception, Barrier Methods & Reproductive Health
cheatSheet.summary: [IB MYP 5 • Sciences] Contraception, Barrier Methods & Reproductive Health: Exploring Scientific and technical innovation (exploring natural laws and systems) through holistic criteria-based inquiry.
cueQuestions: How does Contraception, Barrier Methods & Reproductive Health model relationships and systems within Scientific and technical innovation?
How do we apply the core principles of Contraception, Barrier Methods & Reproductive Health to analyze experimental data under Criterion B & C?
What real-world ethical, environmental, and technological implications arise under Criterion D for Contraception, Barrier Methods & Reproductive Health?
cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Reproductive health encompasses physical, emotional, and social well-being. Contraceptive methodologies prevent unintended pregnancies: Barrier methods (condoms, diaphragms; prevent sperm entry and protect against STIs), Hormonal methods (oral pills; inhibit ovulation), Intrauterine Devices (IUDs; copper-T blocks implantation), and Surgical methods (vasectomy, tubectomy; irreversible sterilization).
• Global Context Focus: *Scientific and technical innovation (exploring natural laws and systems)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$\text{Contraception: Barrier (STIs Protection)} + \text{Hormonal} + \text{IUD} + \text{Surgical (Sterilization)}$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: Condoms are the only contraceptive method that provides dual protection against both pregnancy and Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs like HIV/AIDS, Gonorrhea, Syphilis, HPV).
• Dynamic Mechanism: Copper-T IUD releases copper ions that suppress sperm motility and fertilizing capacity.
• Quantitative Relationship: Surgical sterilization: Vasectomy ties/cuts vas deferens in males; Tubectomy ties/cuts fallopian tubes in females.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:
• Inquirer & Thinker: Home security strategies: Barrier methods put a physical deadbolt on the door; Hormonal methods turn off the power switch inside; Surgical methods permanently disconnect the driveway pipeline.
• Real-World Inquiry: Public health family planning initiatives deploy combined oral contraceptives and barrier distribution to reduce maternal mortality rates.

cheatSheet.summary: [IB MYP 5 • Sciences] Mendel's Laws of Segregation & Independent Assortment: Exploring Orientation in space and time (scale, duration, and human journeys) through holistic criteria-based inquiry.

cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Gregor Mendel discovered the principles of inheritance using Pisum sativum: Law of Segregation (alleles of a gene separate during gametogenesis such that each gamete carries one allele; monohybrid F2 phenotypic ratio 3:1, genotypic ratio 1:2:1) and Law of Independent Assortment (different gene pairs assort independently during gamete formation; dihybrid F2 phenotypic ratio 9:3:3:1).
• Global Context Focus: *Orientation in space and time (scale, duration, and human journeys)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$\text{Monohybrid F2: } 3:1 \text{ (Phenotypic)}, \, 1:2:1 \text{ (Genotypic)}; \quad \text{Dihybrid F2: } 9:3:3:1$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: Dominant allele expresses itself in both homozygous (TT) and heterozygous (Tt) states.
• Dynamic Mechanism: Recessive allele expresses phenotypic trait ONLY in homozygous state (tt).
• Quantitative Relationship: Punnett squares calculate statistical probability ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:
• Inquirer & Thinker: Flipping two independent coins: flipping a quarter (Heads/Tails for height) has zero influence on the outcome of flipping a penny (Heads/Tails for seed color).
• Real-World Inquiry: Modern crop breeding programs use Mendelian marker-assisted selection to breed disease-resistant and drought-tolerant staple crop cultivars.

cheatSheet.title: Chromosomal Sex Determination (XX / XY)
cheatSheet.summary: [IB MYP 5 • Sciences] Chromosomal Sex Determination (XX / XY): Exploring Identities and relationships (mental, physical, and ecological connections) through holistic criteria-based inquiry.
cueQuestions: How does Chromosomal Sex Determination (XX / XY) model relationships and systems within Identities and relationships?
How do we apply the core principles of Chromosomal Sex Determination (XX / XY) to analyze experimental data under Criterion B & C?
What real-world ethical, environmental, and technological implications arise under Criterion D for Chromosomal Sex Determination (XX / XY)?
cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Human sex determination is chromosomal: human cells contain 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of allosomes (sex chromosomes). Females are homogametic (XX, producing only X-bearing eggs); Males are heterogametic (XY, producing 50% X-sperm and 50% Y-sperm). The genetic sex of offspring is determined entirely by the fertilizing paternal sperm, yielding an exact 1:1 (50%) statistical sex ratio.
• Global Context Focus: *Identities and relationships (mental, physical, and ecological connections)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$\text{Female: } 44\text{A} + \text{XX} \implies \text{Egg } (22\text{A}+\text{X}); \quad \text{Male: } 44\text{A} + \text{XY} \implies \text{Sperm } (22\text{A}+\text{X} \text{ or } 22\text{A}+\text{Y})$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: In birds, sex determination is ZZ (male) / ZW (female heterogametic).
• Dynamic Mechanism: In reptiles (crocodiles, turtles), sex determination is environmental (temperature-dependent incubation).
• Quantitative Relationship: The SRY gene on the Y chromosome triggers testis development in human male embryos.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:

cheatSheet.title: Homologous vs Analogous Organs & Speciation
cheatSheet.summary: [IB MYP 5 • Sciences] Homologous vs Analogous Organs & Speciation: Exploring Fairness and development (resource sustainability and ethical responsibility) through holistic criteria-based inquiry.
cueQuestions: How does Homologous vs Analogous Organs & Speciation model relationships and systems within Fairness and development?
How do we apply the core principles of Homologous vs Analogous Organs & Speciation to analyze experimental data under Criterion B & C?
What real-world ethical, environmental, and technological implications arise under Criterion D for Homologous vs Analogous Organs & Speciation?
cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Evolutionary evidence stems from comparative anatomy and fossil records: Homologous organs share identical anatomical structural origin but perform different functions (divergent evolution, e.g. human arm, bird wing, whale flipper); Analogous organs share similar functions but have different structural origins (convergent evolution, e.g. bird wing vs bat wing vs insect wing). Speciation occurs via geographic isolation and reproductive isolation.
• Global Context Focus: *Fairness and development (resource sustainability and ethical responsibility)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$\text{Homologous} \implies \text{Common Ancestry (Divergent)}, \quad \text{Analogous} \implies \text{Similar Niche (Convergent)}$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: Divergent evolution indicates common ancestral descent adapting to different environmental niches.
• Dynamic Mechanism: Convergent evolution shows unrelated lineages developing similar adaptive solutions under similar selective pressures.
• Quantitative Relationship: Fossils (e.g. Archaeopteryx: connecting link between reptiles and birds) provide direct chronological evidence of evolutionary transition.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:
• Inquirer & Thinker: Homologous organs are like smartphones modified into tablets or smartwatches (same core motherboard architecture adapted for different tasks); Analogous organs are like submarines and dolphins (both swim underwater, but one is steel engine machinery and the other is mammalian flesh).
• Real-World Inquiry: Comparative genomics and DNA sequence alignment algorithms construct phylogenetic evolutionary trees linking extinct hominids to modern Homo sapiens.

cheatSheet.title: Lindeman's 10% Trophic Transfer Efficiency
cheatSheet.summary: [IB MYP 5 • Sciences] Lindeman's 10% Trophic Transfer Efficiency: Exploring Globalization and sustainability (interconnected global cycles and human impact) through holistic criteria-based inquiry.
cueQuestions: How does Lindeman's 10% Trophic Transfer Efficiency model relationships and systems within Globalization and sustainability?
How do we apply the core principles of Lindeman's 10% Trophic Transfer Efficiency to analyze experimental data under Criterion B & C?
What real-world ethical, environmental, and technological implications arise under Criterion D for Lindeman's 10% Trophic Transfer Efficiency?
cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Lindeman's 10% Law of trophic efficiency dictates that only approximately 10% of energy entering a trophic level is converted into biomass and transferred to the next higher level; the remaining 90% is dissipated as metabolic respiration, cellular work, and heat loss. Consequently, food chains rarely exceed 4 to 5 trophic steps.
• Global Context Focus: *Globalization and sustainability (interconnected global cycles and human impact)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$E_{n+1} = 0.10 \times E_n, \quad \text{Energy Loss} \approx 90\% \text{ per step}$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: Energy flow in an ecosystem is strictly UNIDIRECTIONAL (from Sun -> Producers -> Primary Consumers -> Apex Predators).
• Dynamic Mechanism: Pyramids of Energy are ALWAYS upright in all ecosystems because energy is irretrievably lost at every trophic step.
• Quantitative Relationship: Producers (green plants) capture only about 1% of total incident solar photon radiation falling on leaves.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:
• Inquirer & Thinker: Passing water down a line of leaky cups: each person spills 90% of the water during transfer, so by the fourth person only a few tiny drops remain in the cup.
• Real-World Inquiry: Agricultural sustainability scientists calculate that plant-based human diets require 90% less land and trophic energy inputs than feeding livestock cattle.

1. **Assuming an energy pyramid can be inverted in aquatic marine ecosystems.**: Assuming an energy pyramid can be inverted in aquatic marine ecosystems.
   • **Remedy / Clarification**: Pyramids of BIOMASS can be inverted in oceans (tiny phytoplankton standing crop feeding large whales), but the Pyramid of ENERGY is ALWAYS upright without exception.

2. Criterion Assessment Check:
• Criterion A (Knowing and Understanding): Explaining biological mechanisms and cellular physiology.
• Criterion B (Inquiring and Designing): Planning controlled biological experiments and sampling methodologies.

cheatSheet.title: Biological Biomagnification in Food Chains
cheatSheet.summary: [IB MYP 5 • Sciences] Biological Biomagnification in Food Chains: Exploring Scientific and technical innovation (exploring natural laws and systems) through holistic criteria-based inquiry.
cueQuestions: How does Biological Biomagnification in Food Chains model relationships and systems within Scientific and technical innovation?
How do we apply the core principles of Biological Biomagnification in Food Chains to analyze experimental data under Criterion B & C?
What real-world ethical, environmental, and technological implications arise under Criterion D for Biological Biomagnification in Food Chains?
cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Biological Biomagnification is the progressive accumulation and increasing concentration of non-biodegradable, lipid-soluble toxic chemicals (e.g. DDT, methylmercury, PCBs, microplastics) at each successively higher trophic level in a food chain because top predators consume large numbers of contaminated prey.
• Global Context Focus: *Scientific and technical innovation (exploring natural laws and systems)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$C_{\text{trophic level } n+1} > C_{\text{trophic level } n}, \quad \text{DDT: } 0.000003\,\text{ppm (Water)} \rightarrow 25\,\text{ppm (Osprey)}$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: Pollutants must be non-biodegradable and fat-soluble (lipophilic) to biomagnify.
• Dynamic Mechanism: Apex predators (e.g. eagles, dolphins, humans) suffer the highest and most lethal pollutant concentrations.
• Quantitative Relationship: DDT bioaccumulation caused severe eggshell thinning in bald eagles and peregrine falcons, driving them to near extinction until banned.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:
• Inquirer & Thinker: Collecting poisonous coins: small fish eat 10 contaminated plankton, big fish eat 10 small fish (holding 100 coins), and the pelican eats 10 big fish, concentrating 1000 poisonous coins in its liver tissues.
• Real-World Inquiry: Environmental toxicology agencies establish maximum permissible contaminant levels (MCL) for seafood based on biomagnification models.

cheatSheet.curriculumTrap:
1. IB Assessment Pitfalls & Misconceptions:
1. **Confusing bioaccumulation (toxic buildup within a single organism over its lifetime) with biomagnification (increasing concentration across multiple trophic levels).**: Confusing bioaccumulation (toxic buildup within a single organism over its lifetime) with biomagnification (increasing concentration across multiple trophic levels).
   • **Remedy / Clarification**: Bioaccumulation happens within ONE individual; Biomagnification happens UP THE FOOD CHAIN across trophic levels.

2. Criterion Assessment Check:
• Criterion A (Knowing and Understanding): Explaining biological mechanisms and cellular physiology.
• Criterion B (Inquiring and Designing): Planning controlled biological experiments and sampling methodologies.

workedExample.problem: [IB MYP Criteria A & C Question • Level 7-8] Explain why apex fish-eating birds of prey (like ospreys) had DDT concentrations nearly 10 million times higher than the surrounding lake water.
steps: Step 1 [Criterion A]: DDT runoff enters lake water at trace concentrations (0.000003 ppm).
Step 2 [Criterion B]: Phytoplankton absorb DDT, accumulating it in lipid membranes (0.04 ppm).
Step 3 [Criterion C]: Zooplankton eat thousands of phytoplankton, concentrating DDT further (0.2 ppm).
Step 4 [Criterion A]: Small fish eat zooplankton (2.0 ppm); large fish eat small fish (5.0 ppm).
Step 5 [Criterion B]: Apex birds consume tons of fish over their lifespans, storing non-biodegradable DDT in body fat at up to 25.0 ppm, disrupting calcium metabolism and eggshell calcification.

cheatSheet.title: Solid Waste Management & Biogas Digestion
cheatSheet.summary: [IB MYP 5 • Sciences] Solid Waste Management & Biogas Digestion: Exploring Orientation in space and time (scale, duration, and human journeys) through holistic criteria-based inquiry.
cueQuestions: How does Solid Waste Management & Biogas Digestion model relationships and systems within Orientation in space and time?
How do we apply the core principles of Solid Waste Management & Biogas Digestion to analyze experimental data under Criterion B & C?
What real-world ethical, environmental, and technological implications arise under Criterion D for Solid Waste Management & Biogas Digestion?
cheatSheet.mainNotes:
**1. Foundational Concept & Global Inquiry (Criterion A & D)**:
• Core Definition: Sustainable municipal solid waste management utilizes the 5Rs (Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repurpose, Recycle) and biochemical valorization: anaerobic methanogenic digestion converts biodegradable organic waste into methane-rich Biogas (65% CH4) and nutrient-rich slurry fertilizer.
• Global Context Focus: *Orientation in space and time (scale, duration, and human journeys)*.
• Key Governing Formula: $$\text{Organic Biomass} \xrightarrow{\text{Hydrolysis/Acidogenesis}} \text{Volatile Fatty Acids} \xrightarrow{\text{Methanogens}} \text{CH}_4 (65\%) + \text{CO}_2 (30\%) + \text{H}_2\text{S}$$

**2. Investigation & Mathematical/Scientific Modeling (Criterion B & C)**:
• Key Observation: Biodegradable waste (food scraps, paper, manure) breaks down naturally via microbial action.
• Dynamic Mechanism: Non-biodegradable waste (plastics, glass, toxic e-waste) persists for centuries and must be recycled or safely sequestered in sanitary landfills.
• Quantitative Relationship: Biogas digestion provides dual ecological benefits: renewable zero-carbon energy and elimination of open-air landfill methane emissions.

**3. IB Learner Profile & Conceptual Analogy**:
• Inquirer & Thinker: An anaerobic biogas digester is like an artificial mechanical cow stomach: anaerobic microbes chew up raw vegetable food waste without oxygen to belch out clean-burning methane cooking gas.
• Real-World Inquiry: Municipal wastewater treatment facilities and dairy farms capture biogas from sewage sludge digesters to generate on-site combined heat and electrical power (CHP).

1. IB Assessment Pitfalls & Misconceptions:
1. **Allowing oxygen into an anaerobic biogas digester chamber.**: Allowing oxygen into an anaerobic biogas digester chamber.
   • **Remedy / Clarification**: Methanogenic archaebacteria are obligate anaerobes; exposure to atmospheric oxygen halts methane fermentation completely.

2. Criterion Assessment Check:
• Criterion A (Knowing and Understanding): Explaining biological mechanisms and cellular physiology.
• Criterion B (Inquiring and Designing): Planning controlled biological experiments and sampling methodologies.

workedExample.problem: [IB MYP Criteria A & C Question • Level 7-8] List the four sequential biochemical stages of anaerobic digestion in a modern biogas digester plant.
steps: Step 1 [Criterion A]: 1. Hydrolysis: Complex polymers (proteins, carbohydrates, lipids) are broken down into soluble monomers by extracellular enzymes.
Step 2 [Criterion B]: 2. Acidogenesis: Acid-forming bacteria convert monomers into volatile fatty acids (VFAs), alcohols, and CO2.
Step 3 [Criterion C]: 3. Acetogenesis: Acetogenic bacteria transform VFAs into acetic acid, CO2, and H2.
Step 4 [Criterion A]: 4. Methanogenesis: Methanogenic archaea convert acetic acid and H2/CO2 into methane gas (\(\text{CH}_4\)) and carbon dioxide.
workedExample.result: Solution: Hydrolysis -> Acidogenesis -> Acetogenesis -> Methanogenesis. [Criterion A-C Level 8 Achievement]
